The Dolphins have started strong this fall, running their record to 2-0 with dominant performances in back-to-back weeks. Gulf Shores opened the season with a 30-21 victory…
item.content:encoded:
Gulf Shores High School head coach Mark Hudspeth has earned JBT Power Coach of the Week honors for the third week of the Friday Night Football season, according to WKRG News 5.

The Dolphins have started strong this fall, running their record to 2-0 with dominant performances in back-to-back weeks. Gulf Shores opened the season with a 30-21 victory over Parklane Academy before shutting down St. Paul's last Friday night with a commanding 34-10 win.

Hudspeth's squad continues to build momentum heading into the remainder of the regular season.

item.content:encoded:
A 13-year-old boy is facing felony charges after authorities say he made threats targeting three schools in Okaloosa County, according to reporting from WKRG News 5.

Okaloosa County sheriff's deputies did not immediately release additional details about the nature of the threats or which schools were targeted. The investigation remains ongoing as authorities work to determine the circumstances surrounding the allegations.

School safety threats have become a serious concern for law enforcement across Florida and the nation. Students making threats against educational facilities typically face criminal charges, which can include felony counts depending on the specifics of what was communicated.

The Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office has not yet announced whether additional charges or arrests are expected as part of this investigation.

item.title: Woman Gets Time Served in Child Abduction Case After Mexico Flight
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A woman who took her daughter across the border to Mexico has been sentenced to time served in an international parental kidnapping case, according to WKRG News 5. Haley Harris was convicted after she fled Alabama with her child in September 2025, crossing into Mexico with the girl. The case drew authorities from multiple jurisdictions as law…
item.content:encoded:
A woman who took her daughter across the border to Mexico has been sentenced to time served in an international parental kidnapping case, according to WKRG News 5.

Haley Harris was convicted after she fled Alabama with her child in September 2025, crossing into Mexico with the girl. The case drew authorities from multiple jurisdictions as law enforcement worked to locate and recover the child.

Harris received a sentence of time served, meaning the time she already spent in custody counted as her full punishment. The resolution concludes a case that highlighted the serious federal crimes involved when a custodial parent unlawfully removes a child across international lines.

Details about the circumstances surrounding the abduction and the child's recovery were not immediately available.

item.content:encoded:
Drivers heading to Eglin Air Force Base should plan for delays this week. According to base officials, Highway 85 and State Road 123 will experience intermittent closures on Wednesday as the base conducts testing operations.

The temporary road closures are expected to cause traffic disruptions for anyone traveling through or accessing the base. Eglin officials recommend that commuters and visitors allow extra time for their trips and consider alternative routes if possible during the testing window.

Base leadership has not specified the exact timing of the closures or provided details about the nature of the testing. Motorists are advised to monitor local traffic conditions and check Eglin AFB's official communications for any updates or changes to the closure schedule.

item.content:encoded: Cat Country 98.7 and the Cat Pak Morning Show have both been nominated for 2026 Country Music Association awards. Cat Country is one of five radio stations nationwide nominated for Radio Station of the Year, while the Cat Pak Morning Show is one of five nominees for Broadcast Personality of the Year. WYCT previously won Station of the Year in 2017, 2019 and 2024, while the Cat Pak Morning Show won Broadcast Personality of the Year in 2022. The winners will be announced during the 60th Annual CMA Awards, which airs Nov. 19 on ABC.

item.content:encoded:
Two Pensacola residents have been handed prison sentences for their roles in distributing fentanyl, according to a Department of Justice announcement.

25-year-old Adrian Dion Pettaway Jr. was among those convicted in the case, which represents another significant drug trafficking prosecution in the Pensacola area. Federal authorities have intensified efforts against fentanyl distribution networks across Northwest Florida in recent years, as the synthetic opioid continues to drive overdose deaths nationally and locally.

The sentencing comes as law enforcement agencies throughout Escambia County work to combat the spread of illicit fentanyl. The drug has become a major public health concern, with emergency responders frequently responding to overdose calls involving the powerful narcotic.

Details on the specific prison sentences and the identity of the second defendant were not immediately available, but the case underscores ongoing federal prosecution of drug trafficking operations in the Pensacola region.

item.content:encoded:
Northwest Florida's defense and shipbuilding sectors are getting a financial boost through several newly awarded grants aimed at strengthening the region's workforce and national security capabilities.

According to Gov. Ron DeSantis's office, the grants directed to Gulf Coast organizations will support training programs and industry development in the area's vital defense manufacturing and shipbuilding fields. The funding underscores the region's strategic importance to Florida's economy and the nation's defense infrastructure.

The awards come as Northwest Florida continues to position itself as a hub for defense-related industries, building on the region's existing military presence and industrial base. Local organizations receiving the grants are expected to use the funding to expand training opportunities and strengthen the pipeline of skilled workers for defense contractors and shipbuilders operating in the area.

Details on specific grant amounts and organizations have not yet been released, according to reporting from WKRG News 5.

item.content:encoded:
A Bay Minette woman faces animal cruelty charges after authorities discovered one dead dog and confiscated 15 others from her home, according to the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office.

The arrest followed an animal welfare investigation that uncovered conditions severe enough to warrant both criminal charges and removal of the animals from the property. One dog was found deceased at the residence, leading to the cruelty charge.

All 15 dogs have been taken into custody as part of the ongoing investigation. The Baldwin County Sheriff's Office did not immediately provide additional details about the specific charges or condition of the surviving animals.

item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office and Gulf Breeze Police Department have announced they're discontinuing use of automated license plate reader cameras, according to WKRG News 5.

The decision marks a shift in enforcement technology for both agencies, though details on the specific reasons behind the move were not immediately available. Automated license plate readers have become increasingly common in law enforcement across Florida, capturing vehicle registration information to help track stolen vehicles and identify suspects.

It's unclear whether the agencies plan to pursue alternative surveillance or tracking methods, or if budget, privacy concerns, or other operational factors influenced the decision. Neither agency has released a detailed statement explaining the timing or rationale for discontinuing the system.

NewsRadio Pensacola will continue to seek more information from both the sheriff's office and Gulf Breeze police about the decision and any impact on their investigative operations.

item.content:encoded: Escambia County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Images of the Cat in the Hat character being used to signal threats against schools have circulated in Escambia, Okaloosa, and possibly Santa Rosa counties in recent days. Officials say the meme is being treated as a credible threat indicator whenever it appears, even though no incidents have materialized locally. Deputies are reminding parents to talk with their kids about not sharing this kind of content, even as a joke, since it can trigger a major law enforcement and school security response regardless of intent.

item.title: UWF Students Help Wildlife Sanctuary Plan Relocation Campaign
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- University of West Florida marketing students conducted a professional-level feasibility study for the Wildlife Sanctuary of Northwest Florida, helping the organization plan a capital campaign to move out of a chronic flood zone. Students surveyed Escambia and Santa Rosa County residents, finding the community has…
item.content:encoded: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- University of West Florida marketing students conducted a professional-level feasibility study for the Wildlife Sanctuary of Northwest Florida, helping the organization plan a capital campaign to move out of a chronic flood zone. Students surveyed Escambia and Santa Rosa County residents, finding the community has the capacity to support the campaign, especially through emotional, animal-centered storytelling and targeting prior donors. Professor James Mead says the research would normally cost fifty-thousand dollars or more if done by a professional firm. The Wildlife Sanctuary has since launched its capital campaign and applied for additional grant funding to relocate to a new ten-acre campus.

item.content:encoded: A newly approved treatment is giving doctors another tool in fighting pancreatic cancer, one of the most difficult cancers to manage. According to WKRG News 5, the FDA approval represents a potentially significant step forward for patients facing this aggressive disease. Pancreatic cancer remains notoriously challenging to treat, with historically low survival rates compared to many other cancer types. The new option could expand the arsenal available to oncologists treating local patients diagnosed with the disease. For West Florida residents or their families dealing with a pancreatic cancer diagnosis, discussing this new treatment option with their medical team may be worthwhile. The development underscores ongoing efforts in the medical community to improve outcomes for one of cancer's most formidable opponents.

The Florida Republican's Lake America Act would need to pass both chambers of Congress to become law. Lake Ontario is the smallest of the five Great Lakes and sits primarily on the U.S.-Canada…
item.content:encoded: Congressman Jimmy Patronis has introduced legislation that would officially change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America, according to WKRG News 5. The Florida Republican's Lake America Act would need to pass both chambers of Congress to become law. Lake Ontario is the smallest of the five Great Lakes and sits primarily on the U.S.-Canada border. The reasoning behind Patronis's proposal and its likelihood of passage remain unclear. If approved, it would represent a significant change to one of North America's most recognizable geographic features.

item.title: Escambia Sheriff Discusses Flock Camera Fallout, Murder Charge, and Vape Shop Burglaries
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Escambia County Sheriff Chip Simmons joined Pensacola's Morning News Tuesday with updates on several active cases, along with his agency's response to a state order that's forcing changes to its license plate reader program. Flock Cameras Simmons says Governor Ron DeSantis's order requiring the removal of automated license plate readers from state…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Sheriff Chip Simmons joined Pensacola's Morning News Tuesday with updates on several active cases, along with his agency's response to a state order that's forcing changes to its license plate reader program.


Flock Cameras

Simmons says Governor Ron DeSantis's order requiring the removal of automated license plate readers from state road rights-of-way is going to hit ECSO's network hard. He says roughly a third of the agency's cameras sit on state roads, and pulling them out will meaningfully weaken a system that depends on being complete to function well. The Florida Department of Transportation gave agencies 30 days to remove the cameras or have state crews do it for them.


Simmons says his cameras haven't been switched off yet and won't be used any less in the meantime — if a crime happens today and a license plate reader can help, his office is going to use it. But he says the agency is actively weighing whether to keep running a smaller, less effective network once the state road cameras come down, or pause the whole program until there's more legal clarity, an approach several other Florida sheriff's offices, including Duval, Volusia, and Seminole counties, have already taken.


Second-Degree Murder Charge

A woman told deputies she shot a man in self-defense during an incident at a Pine Forest Road apartment, but Simmons says the investigation didn't support her claim. Ashanti Brown is now charged with second-degree murder. Simmons says Brown allegedly took a doorbell camera and her cell phone from the scene and discarded them in a ditch in Santa Rosa County — a detail he says undercuts her account, since someone acting in self-defense would typically want that evidence reviewed, not hidden. Investigators are still working to access the data on the discarded devices. Simmons says the charge could be upgraded depending on what they find, though that would likely require evidence the shooting was planned or an ambush.


Vape Shop Burglaries

Deputies arrested three people in connection with five vape shop burglaries reported over the past couple weeks near Nine Mile Road. Simmons says vape shops and marijuana dispensaries have become a recent target locally, with burglars likely assuming the businesses keep cash or product on hand overnight. He says the arrests came after investigators worked the pattern of break-ins.


Other Cases

A 27-year-old man reported being shot in the calf near Wedgwood but refused to tell deputies what happened, leading Simmons to suspect the wound may have been self-inflicted. Simmons also addressed a Cat in the Hat meme circulating online that's being used to signal school threats, with incidents reported in Escambia, Okaloosa, and possibly Santa Rosa counties. He says no threats materialized locally, but his office treats every one seriously given the disruption and fear they can cause, even when they turn out to be a joke.
